<img class="tool-icon" src="../../../../images/tekla/tools/urebarshape.svg" alt="" width="48" height="48" style="display:block;margin:0 0 1rem;background:#fff;border-radius:8px;padding:4px" />

{{% callout type="info" %}}
**Where to find it:** Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → `uRebarShape` (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Rebar block)
{{% /callout %}}

Changes the shape of rebar: offsets or flattens it, flips its cover, bakes its offsets or explodes its hooks into the shape, or brings its bends and custom hooks to the reinforcement catalog. It is the shape half of what the findings of [uRebarInspector](../../model-plugins/urebarinspector/) point to; the hook half is [uRebarHook](../urebarhook/). It replaces the Shape and Standards tabs of uRebarInspector 26.1.18 and earlier, and uRebarShapeTools.

**How to use:**

1.  Select the rebar in Tekla, or leave the selection empty. Choose the operation in the dialog and click **Apply**. The preselected rebar is used once; after that you pick rebar and finish each pick with a middle-click. <kbd>Esc</kbd> ends the command.
2.  Each round changes the picked rebar in one step, so one Undo takes it back, and the status line says how many objects were changed. Objects that were not changed are listed with the reason after the round.

| Operation | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Offset** | Moves the bar within its own plane by *Distance* (mm, negative the other way), like changing its cover; it never leaves the plane. The plane is the best-fit plane of each polygon, or one you define with *Pick 3 points*; a tapered group only takes the direction of a picked plane, through each polygon's own centre. A distance of 0 is refused. |
| **Flatten** | Puts every point of the bar onto one plane (best fit, or three picked points). A spiral is not planar and is skipped. |
| **Flip cover** | Negates every on-plane offset, so the cover moves to the other side of the input line. |
| **Bake offsets** | Moves the input points onto the bar Tekla draws: the on-plane offsets, the cover or leg length at both ends and a single bar's from-plane offset become part of the points and are set to 0. Hooks stay hooks; a group keeps its range, spacing and start and end covers. |
| **Explode hooks** | Does the same and turns each hook into the last leg of the polygon, with its bend radius, and switches the hooks off. |
| **To catalog** | Compares every bend radius and hook with the reinforcement catalog (`rebar_database.inp`) row for the bar's grade, size and usage, and sets what differs to the catalog values. *Usage* chooses the row: Auto takes tie or stirrup for a closed bar and main bars otherwise. *Bends*: Not changed; Raise to minimum (a radius below the catalog minimum gets the catalog radius, a larger one is kept); Set to catalog (every corner gets the catalog radius). *Hook radius* and *Hook length* switch the correction of custom hooks on and off, and at least one of the three must be on. |

Bake offsets and Explode hooks work on single bars and plain polygonal groups (one or two polygons), and never move a bar: the bars are read back after the change, and if they moved the bar is put back and listed. A bar that belongs to a component is left alone, because the component would write it back. To catalog only changes custom hooks: a hook that uses a standard 90, 135 or 180 degree shape already follows the catalog, and a custom hook at another angle has no catalog length. A tapered group is compared on its first polygon. It is the same comparison the BEND\_RADIUS and HOOK rules of the Inspector use, so a bar the Inspector flags is the bar To catalog corrects.

Rebar sets are read-only and are listed as skipped for every operation. Reversing the direction of a bar or of a group's range is [uSwap](../uswap/).

{{% callout type="warning" %}}
After a native failure partial changes can remain: inspect the reported object and use Undo.
{{% /callout %}}
